concept.name: The Island Money Mystery
concept.secret_fact: Money only has value because people agree to use it in a community.
concept.goal: The student must understand that value comes from community trust, not from the object itself.
concept.story_intro: Ugh, I found a huge pile of sparkly coins on the playground, but they're dusty and nobody seems to want them! If I tried to trade them for a yummy cookie, the kid just shrugged. Does this pile of coins actually have any value if no one knows what to do with them?
concept.story_bridge: Wow! So the shiny coins aren't magic, but they work because everyone here knows they are good for trading. That makes sense!
concept.evaluator_ground_truth: Money needs a community (or group of people) to agree that it is valuable for trading.
concept.verification_scenario: Okay, so if we take all these shiny coins and fly to a tiny island where there are NO houses or people, I bet they'd still work! I can trade them to the palm trees for coconuts, right?
concept.verification_ground_truth: Money needs people and a system of trade. Without a community, the coins are just metal; nobody accepts them.

concept.name: Value Isn't Just Paper
concept.secret_fact: Value doesn't come from an object itself, but from people agreeing to use it.
concept.goal: The student must understand that the value of money (or any tool) comes from the community's belief and ability to exchange it.
concept.story_intro: I was digging in the backyard yesterday, and I found this shiny, old box filled with pennies! My brother says I can spend them at the store. But wait, if we're on a trip and we only have grapes and sticks to trade, are the pennies any good? Are they really 'money' if nobody accepts them?
concept.story_bridge: Wow, if we can only trade things we both need, we are really good at trading! It's like we understand what things are actually worth to each other.
concept.evaluator_ground_truth: Money is a 'social contract'—it only works because people in a community agree that it has value and will accept it in exchange for things.
concept.verification_scenario: So, if I had my pile of pennies and my sister found a giant pile of those same pennies on a deserted island, would either pile be 'money'? Because there are no shops and no neighbors to trade with, those pennies wouldn't be worth anything at all, right?
concept.verification_ground_truth: Money needs a community (people to trade with) to give it value. Without people agreeing to exchange things, the object (the pennies) is just metal and has no value.
